newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Flextech up 7.0 pct on chip package news.
newsitem.headline: Flextech up 7.0 pct on chip package news.

text.p: Shares in electronics and industrial distributor Flextech Holdings jumped seven percent, or seven cents, to Singapore $1.06 after a buy recommendation and news of a licensing agreement with a U.S. electronics group.
DBS Investment research said in a note to clients earlier on Wednesday it was repeating its buy recommendation on the company in view of "the explosive growth of the company".

DBS said Flextech would gain from a licencing agreement signed recently by its unit, Flexera, and U.S.-based Tessera Corp. Under the deal, Flexera would be given the right to make a new type of packaging for microchips and circuitry.

As a result, Flexera would set up a 14,000 sq ft facility to manufacture chip scale packaging products. Initial production estimates were 10 million pieces per month from June 1997, increasing to 18 million pieces per month by 1998, it said.
"In view of the explosive growth of the company, we remain positive on its longer term fundamentals and reiterate our buy recommendation," DBS said.
Dealers said news of the deal had just reached the market.
